name: Bermuda
summary: Bermuda has no forced heirship and gives full freedom to leave the estate by will, though a spouse, child or grandchild can ask the court for provision. Trusts are central and protected against foreign forced-heirship claims. The Hague Trusts Convention is in force for Bermuda; a private foundation law was reported as absent.
family_claims: Part III of the Succession Act 1974 allows an application for financial provision from the estate by a spouse, former spouse who has not remarried, and a child or grandchild maintained by the deceased (commentary also lists parents and grandparents). A spouse needs only show provision is reasonable; others must show maintenance is reasonable in the circumstances. Cohabitees are excluded.
foreign_law_note: No source read states Bermuda's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate; estate tax is mentioned only for 'Bermudian property'. Common-law rule: movables follow the law of the domicile, land follows local law. Not confirmed in local statute for this jurisdiction.
trust_note: Bermuda is on the UK's HCCH extension list (in force 1 January 1992). Trusts (Special Provisions) Act 1989, s. 11 (restated in 2020) bars attacks on a trust under foreign heirship law. A 2019 Chambers guide says Bermuda has no foundations law and does not recognise foundations.
open_questions: The foundations statement dates from 2019; later changes were not checked.
Section numbers and time limit for Part III claims not read.
Estate tax rules for Bermudian property were mentioned but not detailed.
